blindComparison: A stranger picks Ghost of Tsushima, and the single specific reason is that our objects are not fastened to the floor and our floor has holes in it. Crop `probe crop shots/phone-wide-r17v2.png 0.4198,0.7795,0.1603,0.2000` and look at 1:1: each stone lantern sits at the centre of a warm disc whose BRIGHTEST pixels are exactly at the contact point -- ground ring (1141,1084 42x16) p50 105.0 against open plateau (1420,1084 42x16) p50 35.8, 2.93x brighter where the object touches -- with no contact darkening, no ambient occlusion at the base and no cast shadow, repeated across roughly fifteen lanterns, three torii, two pavilions and the honden. Tsushima's equivalent shot nails every one of those objects down with a long raking shadow and a tight dark seam. Then crop `probe crop shots/phone-hero-r17v2.png 0.4897,0.8034,0.1343,0.1026`: three hard-edged, perfectly featureless black voids lie in the lit flagstone, (1413,989 51x23) at meanRGB [3.0,3.0,4.1] p50 3.1 detail 2.54 against identical flagstone 160 px away at p50 41.3 detail 8.62 -- 7.5% of its neighbour, no penumbra, no caster, no texture inside. The `torii` frame on its own would survive the comparison: vermilion lacquer, real gold-leaf fittings, a twisted shimenawa, a genuine blue dome with cloud, snow ridges behind. `sun` would nearly survive on the wet-stone specular path alone. The set does not, because two of five frames are frames no shipped title would put on a store page.
godRayVerdict: Volumetric shafts still do not read as light, in either frame, and I am saying that on a verified instrument rather than on the eye alone. In `valley` I located the disc by centroid of pixels >= 246 at (950,56), confirmed by crop `0.3910,0.0085,0.1264,0.2051` that a bamboo culm and leaf spray occupy r = 40..260 px from the disc across theta = -33..+47 deg, and confirmed by crop `0.5036,0.0214,0.0750,0.3376` that the annulus at r = 500 px over theta = 0..24 deg is 100% clean sky -- so that arc lies radially outward of a real, thin, high-contrast occluder and nothing else. Sampled at 1 deg with a 3x3 mean it reads 207.53 to 220.51, mean |high-pass at lag 9| = 1.298 and maximum |high-pass| = 3.834 code values: a smooth monotone falloff with no angular structure whatever, where a shaft that reads as light needs 10 to 25. By eye at 1:1 the same is true of `sun`: the sky inside 300 px of the disc is bounded by the shimenawa, three shide strips, two paper lanterns and the left upright, and outward of every one of them it is an unbroken radial gradient. The wash half of the r16 finding was genuinely fixed; the differential half was not, exactly as this round's own owner reported.
gateVerdict: The `sun` pctAbove240 breach is NOT a tonal fault -- it is the correct consequence of the composition and the guard is the wrong instrument. I gridded the population 12x6: at >= 240 (my measure: 2.893%) it is confined to two columns at x-frac 0.58..0.75 and rows 0..3, i.e. the sun disc, its bloom halo and the two paper lanterns, plus 6.4% of one bottom cell which is the specular sun path on wet cobble; at >= 250 the share is only 0.455% and is essentially the disc alone. That is a soft, wide, non-blown falloff around a real sun disc, which is what ARCHITECTURE 5.7 asks for; a 0.5%-above-240 guard written for a frame with no disc in it cannot be applied to a frame whose subject IS the disc. The `valley` black-gate breach is different, and my answer is: the gate is measuring the wrong thing, but there is a real fault next to it. p0.1 = 19.0 and 0.057% below code 16 (against `hero` 9.25% and `torii` 9.40% from the same build) is genuinely explained by the composition -- a backlit hazy grove contains no deep architectural void -- and re-deepening the black point would simply re-create round 16's crush, which this round correctly reversed. Do not chase p0.1 on `valley`. The real fault is local: the grove has no tonal recession at all between its depth planes (finding 6), so the frame reads flat for a reason that lowering the black point would not fix.
notesOnApparatus: Candidate findings I killed by cropping or re-probing, before filing: (1) 'god rays are working in `hero`' -- the two bright radial streaks under the shimenawa at (1800,470 420x260) looked like shafts at reduced size; the 1:1 crop shows they are the shide paper strips themselves, lit and hanging. Not light. (2) `sun` box (1240,290 440x280), which I had picked as a clean-sky god-ray probe between the rope and the disc, contains both paper lanterns and three shide strips on crop. Discarded, no number quoted from it. (3) A `valley` arc at r=400 and r=300 from the disc gave large angular modulation (max |high-pass| 8.9 and 40.5) and would have read as a god-ray success -- the crop `probe crop shots/phone-valley-r17v2.png 0.4265,0.2479,0.1106,0.1026` shows the tail of both arcs crossing a bamboo leaf spray. This is the round-16 failure exactly, and it is why only the r=500 arc is quoted. My 'G >= R' sky test did NOT catch it: a sunlit bamboo culm is also R>G>B. Colour tests are not a substitute for looking. (4) 'the shadow side is warm everywhere, never the contract's cool #4a6b8f' -- my `sun` box (700,950 400x180) read [75.2,58.1,52.8] but the crop shows it straddling both sides of the terminator; the shadow half alone, (1010,1055 180x100), reads [50.0,50.1,55.7] with B exceeding R, which is correct and cool. The finding survives only for `wide`, where I could show the direction of travel. (5) 'the `torii` plaza has a legible cast shadow / lit split' -- my pair (1450,1090) p50 31.3 and (1750,1090) p50 26.7 has the 'lit' box darker than the 'shadow' box, i.e. I had them backwards. Not filed. (6) A hero sky guard box at (1580,240 140x80) that I intended as a clean-sky control has p1 0.3 and lumaSpread 191.7 -- it contains the torii crossbeam. Replaced with (1823,23 354x70), cropped and confirmed clean (detail 0.44). (7) IMPORTANT for whoever verifies finding 2: the r=130 arc that round 17's OPENING verdict specifies as the god-ray acceptance instrument is not a valid instrument. Around the measured `sun` disc at (1505,524) the sampled sector theta = -85..+85 deg contains no occluder at any radius below 130 px -- there is nothing between the disc and the arc to cast into it -- so a physically correct god-ray pass would still measure flat there. It measures 233.61 to 242.34, mean |high-pass| 0.467, and that number means nothing. `sun` is roughly three-quarters occluded and I could not construct ANY uncontaminated arc in it that sits radially outward of an occluder; that is why finding 2's acceptance is written on `valley`. (8) Measurement harness: every number here comes from tools/probe.mjs's own decodePNG/cut/stats, imported, never re-decoded, so the 3-byte/4-byte stride bug cannot occur. I cross-checked my pixel-coordinate wrapper against the probe.mjs CLI on region 0.2,0.3,0.1,0.1 of `hero` and every field agrees to the digit (meanRGB [151.3,102.9,109.2], p50 122.6, detail 10.33), and I re-ran two of my findings' boxes through the fractional CLI to confirm the fraction/pixel round-trip lands on the same box. (9) `detail` is used in this review only for fine surface texture, never for shafts, sky gradient or cloud.

findings.problem: Three hard-edged, completely featureless near-black voids lie in the lit flagstone of the near-foreground plaza, directly under and beside the shot's focal stone lanterns. They are amoeba/keyhole shaped with a razor boundary, no penumbra, no caster above them, and the flagstone texture stops dead at their edge. Measured on THIS build: (1413,989 51x23) meanRGB [3.0,3.0,4.1], luma p50 3.1, p99 7.4, detail 2.54. Identical flagstone 160 px to the left, (1253,989 51x23): meanRGB [52.5,40.1,38.0], p50 41.3, detail 8.62 -- the void is 7.5% of its neighbour. A second at (1557,989 38x18): [4.5,4.8,6.4], p50 3.9. A third and larger at (1296,980 127x59): [11.7,9.3,10.0], p50 3.4, detail 4.02, against its own left neighbour (1114,980 127x59) at p50 33.8, detail 7.96. See all three at 1:1 with `node tools/probe.mjs crop shots/phone-hero-r17v2.png 0.4897,0.8034,0.1343,0.1026`. CRITICAL AND UNCHANGED: against shots/phone-hero-r16v1.png these boxes read p50 3.1 / 4.0 / 3.6 and detail 2.53 / 3.09 / 4.00 -- byte-identical to two decimal places. Round 17 did not touch these pixels. Note also that adjacent dark shapes in the same crop ARE legitimate lantern cast shadows -- (1300,960 150x40) p50 16.3, detail 5.65, with texture inside and the correct 4.33x-height downsun offset -- so the voids are a different population from the shadows sitting beside them, and the difference is visible at 1:1.
findings.why: A shipped title does not have holes in the floor of a marketing frame. The eye reads them as missing geometry or a broken decal before it reads anything else in the lower third, and they sit under the focal object of the shot. They are also darker than this scene's own ambient floor permits: round 15 measured the fill-only plaza at p50 21.0 and these are at 3.1, so light is being removed below what an unlit surface under this sky can be.
findings.fix: Eliminate the voids so no plaza region falls below the material's fill floor and so the flagstone texture is visible inside them. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `hero`: `probe stats shots/phone-hero-rN.png 0.5581,0.8453,0.0201,0.0197` must return p50 >= 22 AND detail >= 5.0; `0.5119,0.8376,0.0502,0.0504` must return p50 >= 20 AND detail >= 6.0. GUARD against faking with a global lift: the neighbour box `0.4949,0.8453,0.0201,0.0197` must stay within p50 41.3 +/- 15% (35.1 to 47.5), and whole-frame p50 must stay within 75.8 +/- 8% (69.7 to 81.9). CHECK PERFORMED: I cropped `0.4897,0.8034,0.1343,0.1026` at native and looked -- both target boxes land inside voids, the guard box lands on lit cobble with visible joints; and the two target boxes total 51x23 + 127x59 = 8,666 px = 0.29% of the 2,962,440 px frame, so lifting them from p50 ~3 to ~24 moves the frame MEAN by 0.29% x 21 = 0.06 codes and the frame MEDIAN not at all, which makes the structure target and the +/-8% frame guard co-satisfiable by three orders of magnitude.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING -- DISPROVE BEFORE ACTING. Rounds 8 and 15 disproved cascade coverage, cascade weights, the caster set and PCSS for this patch three separate times, and round 15 proved it is not reflectance (4x darker than the darkest albedo Materials.js can produce). Round 16 unprojected it to an opaque ground surface about 2.0 x 2.1 m at world XZ (-6.0, 38.2), beside the path slab by the z=38.5 torii. What is left to ablate one at a time: a decal or contact-darkening card stamped at the wrong intensity; a light/occlusion volume with a negative or over-ranged contribution; an occlusion term applied multiplicatively twice along the chain. That it is byte-identical across two builds says the drawing path was untouched this round, which should narrow the search hard. If the geometry at those coordinates turns out to belong to Props.js or Terrain.js, you own those too.

findings.problem: There are still no volumetric shafts anywhere in the two frames the contract names (ARCHITECTURE 5, non-negotiable #4: 'Volumetric god rays through the torii and bamboo'). The pass delivers a smooth radial halo and nothing else. Verified evidence on `valley`: disc centroid (pixels >= 246) at (950,56). Crop `0.3910,0.0085,0.1264,0.2051` and look -- a bamboo culm and a dense leaf spray occupy r = 40 to 260 px from the disc, spanning theta = -33 to +47 deg, i.e. a thin high-contrast occluder directly in front of the light. Crop `0.5036,0.0214,0.0750,0.3376` and look -- 100% clean sky, no culm, no leaf, no terrain. The arc at r = 500 px inside that clean window, theta = 0 to 24 deg (which is radially outward of the leaf spray), sampled every 1 deg with a 3x3 mean, reads: 208.21 208.82 207.53 212.35 211.61 211.67 213.52 213.98 213.84 213.65 209.60 209.76 211.01 212.21 211.45 214.01 213.81 214.95 219.40 217.31 214.97 213.68 220.51 213.74 214.81. Mean |high-pass at lag 9| = 1.298, maximum |high-pass| = 3.834, total range 13.0 codes and monotone-ish. A leaf blade subtending 3 to 6 deg from the disc would, if the pass were differential, print a 25 to 50 px band at this radius at 10 to 25 codes of contrast. Nothing does. On `sun` the same is true by eye at 1:1: crop the sky inside 300 px of the disc at (1505,524) -- it is bounded by the shimenawa, three shide strips, two paper lanterns and the left upright, and outward of every one of them the sky is an unbroken gradient with no bright or dark bar.
findings.why: A low sun behind a torii and a bamboo sea is the reference titles' signature frame and the single image this whole setting exists to produce. Without discrete shafts the backlit framings read as a lens-flare filter over a still, and the contract lists this as non-negotiable.
findings.fix: Make the pass differential: visible bars where occluders sit, nothing where they do not. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `valley`: re-locate the disc as the centroid of pixels with luma >= 246 (currently (950,56)); sample 25 points at r = 500 px, theta = 0 to 24 deg in 1 deg steps, each a 3x3 mean. The resulting sequence must reach maximum |high-pass at lag 9| >= 10.0 AND mean |high-pass at lag 9| >= 4.0 (currently 3.834 and 1.298). GUARD 1 against faking with gain: the 25-sample mean must stay within 213.0 +/- 5% (202.4 to 223.7). GUARD 2 against re-crushing the shadows, which is what round 16 did and round 17 correctly undid: `valley` share below code 8 must stay <= 2.0% (currently 0.011%), `sun` share below code 8 must stay <= 4.0% (currently 1.639%), and whole-frame `sun` p50 must stay within 106.5 +/- 8% (98.0 to 115.0). CHECK PERFORMED: both crops above were opened at native and confirmed to contain what I say (occluder annulus = culm plus leaves; r=500 window = pure sky); and three dips of 12 codes among 25 samples lower the arc mean by 3 x 12 / 25 = 1.44 codes = 0.68%, comfortably inside the +/-5% gain guard, while the 25 3x3 boxes total 225 px = 0.008% of the frame and therefore cannot move any whole-frame guard at all. Target and both guards are mutually satisfiable. DO NOT use the r=130 arc named in this round's opening verdict -- see notesOnApparatus (7); no occluder lies between the disc and that radius in the sampled sector, so it cannot detect a shaft even if one exists.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Round 15 established that the emitter is not empty (rtGodA 10.2-11.0% non-zero), that sampling converges by N=48, and that the pass smears a 10%-coverage emitter across 99.9% of the frame -- it delivers common mode, not differential. Round 7 established that raising gain makes the frame worse. So the quantity to measure is the pass output's angular variance at fixed radius before and after narrowing the march footprint, not its gain and not its sample count. Round 17 evidently attacked the wash and left the spread: the halo is cleaner and the disc is legible, and the angular variance is still 1.3 codes.

findings.problem: In the establishing shot the plateau -- the lower 55% of the frame -- still has no key/shadow structure and nothing standing on it casts a shadow, and this round's only change to it was a colour rotation that satisfies the previous acceptance criterion's letter while moving away from the contract. The seven hand-verified plateau boxes at y = 825 (60x40, cropped and confirmed to contain only ground) read, new against r16v1: x=150 p50 38.1 (was 38.7); x=340 42.2 (43.0); x=1200 71.3 (71.9); x=1350 75.6 (76.4); x=1700 45.0 (45.7); x=2200 47.6 (48.2); x=2380 48.2 (48.9). Every single box got DARKER by 0.6 to 0.8 codes -- no light was added anywhere. What did change is chroma: previously 5 of 7 had B exceeding R by 5.5 to 12.8 codes (a cool shadow, which is what ARCHITECTURE 5 asks for at magic hour); now 7 of 7 have R exceeding B, e.g. x=150 went [35.9,39.1,48.7] to [40.7,37.5,41.5]. The old acceptance said 'at least 5 of 7 must have mean R > mean B', and that has been met by warming the ambient rather than by lighting the ground, so the frame has lost its cool sky bounce and gained no key. Excluding the two lantern-cluster boxes the remaining five still span only 38.1 to 48.2 = 10.1 codes across 2532 px of frame (was 10.2). Second symptom, unchanged: contact is inverted. Crop `probe crop shots/phone-wide-r17v2.png 0.4198,0.7795,0.1603,0.2000` at 1:1 -- both stone lanterns sit at the centre of a warm disc whose brightest pixels are AT the contact point, ring (1141,1084 42x16) p50 105.0 against open plateau (1420,1084 42x16) p50 35.8, i.e. 2.93x brighter where the object touches the ground, with no contact darkening, no AO at the base and no cast shadow from either. Third symptom: the frame's tonal structure is inverted with depth -- a 700x50 band at x=1500 reads p50 68.7 at y=640 and 31.6 at y=1120, so the nearest ground is the darkest and flattest thing in the shot and the distance is the brightest.
findings.why: Contact shadow is what makes a place feel real; without it every object is a model on a printed floor, which is exactly the reading at thumbnail size. This is the establishing shot -- the frame a store page uses -- and it is the one that most obviously loses the blind comparison against any Tsushima vista where the same low sun rakes across a whole field, throwing every lantern and gate 25 m downsun.
findings.fix: Put a real key on the plateau and real cast shadows under the things standing on it, and restore the cool shadow half rather than warming everything. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `wide`, on the same seven boxes `probe stats shots/phone-wide-rN.png <x>,0.7051,0.0237,0.0342` at x-frac 0.0592 / 0.1343 / 0.4739 / 0.5332 / 0.6714 / 0.8688 / 0.9400: (1) excluding the two lantern-cluster boxes 0.4739 and 0.5332, the remaining five must span >= 25 code values of p50 between max and min (currently 10.1) -- some in sun, some in shadow; (2) of those same five, at least one must have mean R exceeding mean B by >= 15 codes (a warm key) AND at least two must have mean B >= mean R (a cool shadow, per ARCHITECTURE 5's #4a6b8f) -- this replaces the old 'R > B in 5 of 7' criterion, which is what produced the warm rotation; (3) in the crop `0.4198,0.7795,0.1603,0.2000` the base ring `0.4506,0.9265,0.0166,0.0137` must no longer be a local maximum, and some 42x16 box within 40 px of a lantern base on the downsun side must read p50 below the open-plateau value `0.5608,0.9265,0.0166,0.0137` (currently 35.8). GUARD against faking with an exposure or grade change: the massif box `0.760,0.322,0.095,0.051` must keep p50 within 160.0 +/- 6, the bare-hillside box `0.5924,0.2479,0.1659,0.1026` within p50 158.7 +/- 8, and whole-frame `wide` p50 within 90.4 +/- 8% (83.2 to 97.6). CHECK PERFORMED: I cropped all three guard boxes and both are bare rock/hillside containing zero plateau pixels, and I cropped the y=825 row across the full width (three overlapping native crops) and confirmed the seven boxes contain only open ground -- so a 25-code redistribution across the plateau, half up and half down, cannot move either guard box and leaves the frame median where it is; the five structure boxes total 12,000 px = 0.41% of the frame. Target and guards are co-satisfiable.

findings.problem: The pose moved from r = 46.04 m to r = 112.00 m and the frame still contains no readable drop. Crop `probe crop shots/phone-valley-r17v2.png 0.3357,0.7009,0.3555,0.2991` at 1:1: the lower third is a near dirt mound at roughly 3 to 8 m that RISES away from the camera on the right, carrying sparse yellow grass sprigs, backed by a solid wall of bamboo. There is no lip, no cliff face, no valley floor, no water surface (ARCHITECTURE 9 puts WATER_LEVEL 30 m below the plateau) and no layered receding ridges. The only trace of the 319 m drop anywhere in the frame is a hazed sliver of the far side at (730,430 400x150), p50 145.8 saturation 0.434, about 2.0% of the frame, visible between leaf sprays. Separately and in the same crop, at (1130,940 110x60) there is a hard-edged straight-sided completely flat dark-green quad wedged between the mound and the thicket -- meanRGB [59.7,69.7,37.2], detail 3.24 against the dirt 170 px to its right at detail 7.09 -- an untextured flat-colour surface in frame, which ARCHITECTURE 5 non-negotiable #9 forbids outright. Also in the same crop, the dirt itself is smeared pink-tan with scattered blue-black mottling at close range with no aggregate, pebble or wear structure.
findings.why: This is the only framing in the set that carries the premise in ARCHITECTURE 5 -- 'a mountain shrine above a bamboo sea at magic hour... Mist in the valley' -- and it delivers standing waist-deep in a hedge. A 319 m drop that the camera is standing on the lip of, and cannot see, is worse than not having one: the round spent its pose change and bought no pixels. Every Tsushima vista earns its scale from four or five stacked depth bands; this frame has two, both within 30 m.
findings.fix: Make the drop readable from the `valley` pose. findings.problem: The sakura canopy, the largest and most eye-catching object in the frame, is built from large flat-shaded hard-alpha cards and reads as torn crepe paper. At 1:1 (`probe crop shots/phone-hero-r17v2.png 0.0987,0.1538,0.1975,0.2735`) the individual blossom lobes are 40 to 90 px smooth untextured facets on a crown spanning about 700 px, each with a binary alpha edge, visible stair-stepping and a rim of black speckle where the cutout meets the sky. The shading is bimodal with nothing between the two populations: (284,269 51x35) reads meanRGB [117.8,103.8,117.8] saturation 0.154 detail 5.03 (mauve), (380,328 51x35) reads [105.4,78.8,97.4] saturation 0.269 detail 8.39, and lit lobes higher in the crown run salmon. The branches are flat dark strokes drawn on top of the blossom mass rather than passing through it. There is no petal-scale element anywhere and no light passing through any card.
findings.why: It is the first thing the eye lands on in `hero` and the least finished thing in the set -- flat two-tone cutout foliage in front of an otherwise well-textured shrine. Tsushima's blossom trees read as thousands of small translucent elements with the sun coming through them; no amount of quality elsewhere survives that comparison at thumbnail size.
findings.fix: Break the canopy into petal-scale elements with soft silhouette coverage and continuous shading. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `hero`: `probe stats shots/phone-hero-rN.png 0.1122,0.2299,0.0201,0.0299` must return detail >= 12.0 (currently 5.03) and `0.1501,0.2803,0.0201,0.0299` must return detail >= 12.0 (currently 8.39); in the crop `0.0987,0.1538,0.1975,0.2735` no single flat-shaded facet may exceed 25 px across at native. GUARD against faking with grain or sharpening: both boxes' meanRGB must stay within +/-10% per channel of [117.8,103.8,117.8] and [105.4,78.8,97.4], and the clean-sky control `0.72,0.02,0.14,0.06` must keep detail below 1.0 (currently 0.44) so no global sharpen has been applied. CHECK PERFORMED: I cropped 0.0987,0.1538,0.1975,0.2735 at native and both target boxes land inside the canopy (one mauve, one on the mauve/salmon boundary); I cropped 0.72,0.02,0.14,0.06 and it is pure sky, lumaSpread 15.5, no blossom, no torii. The two target boxes total 3,570 px = 0.12% of the frame and the guards are per-box colour plus an off-canopy control, so raising local high-frequency energy inside them cannot conflict with any guard. NOTE, from round 16 and binding here: the card-size change and the texture re-author must land in the SAME round or the canopy regresses -- __blossom is Props.js:_blossomCluster with half-extent 1.00 to 1.68 giving 2.00 to 3.36 m cards on an 11.0 m tree, merged by Level.js, and only the texture is yours. Coordinate.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Two cheap ablations: (a) the card is instanced at several times a real cluster's world size, so a correct texture is simply magnified past its own detail band; (b) the material is alpha-tested (round 16 recorded Props.blossomMaterial as alphaTest 0.36, transparent:false, no A2C and no dither), giving a binary silhouette at every scale, which would explain the stair-stepping and the black edge speckle independently of card size. Measure both before changing either.

findings.problem: The distant tree cover is a ribbon of identical flat green hard-alpha smears with no crown form, no trunk and no depth, and it is the single most damaging element in `wide` after the plateau. At 1:1 (`probe crop shots/phone-wide-r17v2.png 0.0000,0.0000,0.5000,0.5000`, look at the lower half; and `probe crop shots/phone-torii-r17v2.png 0.0592,0.5128,0.2765,0.1368`) the band is a horizontal run of near-identical vertical lozenges, each with a binary alpha edge, all at the same height, all at the same hue, stapled onto the hillside. In `wide` the band (100,380 700x140) measures meanRGB [104.3,100.9,99.2], saturation 0.085, lumaSpread 44.6, detail 5.59 -- it is nearly achromatic, so it has neither the contract's moss #4e6b3c nor any lit-top / shaded-underside modelling; in `torii` the equivalent band (100,620 700x120) measures saturation 0.174. Against the mauve-hazed hillside behind it the band does not recede and does not sit in the same atmosphere -- it reads as lichen on a wall.
findings.why: CRITIC.md priority 6 and 7. This band occupies the whole horizontal width of the establishing frame at the point where the eye travels from the shrine to the mountains, and it is the moment a stranger identifies the image as a game asset rather than a place. Tsushima's mid-distance forests carry crown clumping, a lit side, and a haze ladder that separates each ridge from the next.
findings.fix: Give the distant tree cover crown form and chroma. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `wide`: `probe stats shots/phone-wide-rN.png 0.0395,0.3248,0.2765,0.1197` must return lumaSpread >= 70 (currently 44.6) AND mean saturation >= 0.15 (currently 0.085), with detail staying <= 8.0 (currently 5.59) so the gain is crown form and not grain. In the crop `0.0000,0.0000,0.5000,0.5000` no straight vertical alpha edge longer than 25 px at native may appear in the band. GUARD against faking with a global grade or a sharpen: the bare-hillside box `0.5924,0.2479,0.1659,0.1026` must keep p50 within 158.7 +/- 8 and saturation within 0.118 +/- 0.04, and the clean-sky box `0.898,0.230,0.095,0.051` must keep p50 within 164.8 +/- 10. CHECK PERFORMED: I cropped both guard boxes at native -- the hillside box is bare rock with no tree in it and the sky box is sky -- and I cropped the target region and confirmed it is impostor tree band plus a thin strip of hillside at its top edge. The target box is 98,000 px = 3.3% of the frame; both guards lie entirely outside it, so raising within-box spread and chroma cannot move either. Co-satisfiable.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Round 16 measured that the massif's own kgScaleRamp evaluates to 0.000 at the distances these actually sit at, i.e. the far-range detail machinery is not firing where it was assumed to. Worth one check here: whether the impostor is receiving the same aerial-perspective term as the terrain it stands on, since the band at saturation 0.085 against a hillside at 0.118 suggests it is being desaturated by something other than distance, and whether the impostor card is a single quad per tree with no crown silhouette at all.

findings.problem: Nothing in the bamboo grove recedes: near, mid and far bamboo all sit at one tone and one chroma, so the frame reads as a single depth plane with a backdrop behind it. Three boxes, each cropped and confirmed to contain bamboo only: near (200,780 400x300), culm about 90 px wide, p1 28.3 p50 61.4 saturation 0.698; mid (1450,700 350x250) p1 32.2 p50 64.3 saturation 0.518; far (1900,600 400x150), culm about 25 px wide -- a 3.6x on-screen scale ratio from the near one -- p1 26.9 p50 55.3 saturation 0.673. Across that whole range luma moves by 9 codes in the WRONG direction (the far bamboo is darker than the near) and saturation falls by 0.025, against a sky immediately behind it at p50 210 to 240. The terrain in the same frame does haze correctly -- the far valley wall at (730,430 400x150) reads p50 145.8 saturation 0.434 -- so the ladder exists for terrain and not for foliage. The visible consequence at 1:1 (`probe crop shots/phone-valley-r17v2.png 0.2765,0.3419,0.4344,0.4274`) is that the far canopy is a lumpy tiled green mass at the same weight as the culm two metres from the lens.
findings.why: CRITIC.md priority 5: without aerial perspective a long view reads as a painted backdrop, and this is the frame whose entire job is scale. It is also why the `valley` frame reads flat despite a 198-code lumaSpread -- the range is all in the sky, none of it is in the subject.
findings.fix: Put the bamboo on the same aerial-perspective ladder the terrain is already on. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `valley`, on the three verified boxes `probe stats shots/phone-valley-rN.png` at `0.0790,0.6667,0.1580,0.2564` (near), `0.5727,0.5983,0.1382,0.2137` (mid) and `0.7504,0.5128,0.1580,0.1282` (far): p50 must rise strictly near -> mid -> far with at least 20 codes between near and far (currently it FALLS 6), and saturation must fall strictly near -> mid -> far with at least 0.15 between near and far (currently 0.025). GUARD against faking with global fog, which would re-flatten the frame: the near box must keep saturation >= 0.62 (currently 0.698) and p50 within 61.4 +/- 15%, and whole-frame `valley` saturation must stay >= 0.46 (currently 0.513). EXPLICIT NON-TARGET: do NOT pursue this by lowering the frame's black point. `valley` p0.1 is 19.0 and 0.057% of pixels are below code 16, and deepening that is how round 16 produced the crush that round 17 correctly reversed; the frame's share below code 8 must stay <= 2.0% (currently 0.011%). CHECK PERFORMED: I cropped all three boxes at native -- near is a foreground culm and leaves, mid is thicket, far is a 25-px culm with leaves, none contains sky, ground or the flat green quad. The three total 216,000 px = 7.3% of the frame; the guard is on the near box itself plus a whole-frame saturation floor, and lifting the FAR box while holding the near box fixed raises frame saturation nowhere and lowers it only over the far 2.7% of the frame by at most 0.15 x 0.027 = 0.004, so the 0.46 floor cannot be breached by satisfying the target. Co-satisfiable.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. Two candidates: (a) the foliage material is not consuming the same fog/aerial term the terrain material is, so distance does nothing to it; (b) it is consuming it, but the term is keyed off a depth or world-height input that the instanced card path does not write correctly, so every card is evaluated at the camera's own depth. Distinguish by forcing the aerial term to an extreme value and checking whether the far box moves AT ALL before tuning anything. Note round 8's standing result that valley saturation cannot be moved from Terrain.js -- this finding is about the foliage material, not the ground.

findings.problem: The rectilinear lattice in the sky right of the massif is still there and is measurably MORE visible than in the previous build. Crop `probe crop shots/phone-wide-r17v2.png 0.8491,0.2051,0.1509,0.2222` and look at the right half: roughly vertical hatching crossed by two or three horizontals, about 240x60 px at native around (2274,377). Box `0.898,0.322,0.095,0.051` returns detail 2.20 against 1.14 previously, and its own clean-sky control directly above it, `0.898,0.230,0.095,0.051`, has gone from detail 0.91 / lumaSpread 21.0 to detail 1.54 / lumaSpread 35.9 -- so the structure has strengthened and has begun to reach into the control region too. The same crop also shows fine pale diagonal scratch lines across the massif rock face, which read as the same class of artefact.
findings.why: Straight lines do not occur in sky. Anything rectilinear up there reads as a mesh boundary, a clipmap seam or a projection fault, and it is in the establishing shot.
findings.fix: Remove the rectilinear structure from the sky region. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM `wide`: `probe stats shots/phone-wide-rN.png 0.898,0.322,0.095,0.051` must return detail <= 1.20 and lumaSpread <= 24, and the crop `0.8491,0.2051,0.1509,0.2222` must contain no straight line longer than 40 px above the mountain silhouette. GUARD against faking by blurring the sky: the control box `0.898,0.230,0.095,0.051` must keep detail within 1.54 +/- 0.35, and the massif box `0.760,0.322,0.095,0.051` must keep detail within 3.03 +/- 0.60 so the far terrain is not softened along with it. CHECK PERFORMED: I cropped 0.8491,0.2051,0.1509,0.2222 at native and the lattice is plainly visible in its right half; I cropped the massif guard region and it is bare rock with no plateau and no lattice. Target and both guards are three disjoint boxes totalling 43,380 px = 1.5% of the frame, and the target asks the artefact box to fall to roughly its own control's value, so they are satisfiable by definition.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. It sits directly above the far ridge line at very low contrast, which fits distant terrain or ridge-band geometry showing through the haze rather than being occluded. Confirm by ablating the far-range geometry and re-shooting the same box before touching anything in the sky.

findings.problem: The dressing reads as instanced, not inhabited. Crop `probe crop shots/phone-wide-r17v2.png 0.4198,0.7795,0.1603,0.2000` at 1:1: the two stone lanterns are the same model at the same scale with the same yaw and the same texture orientation, and the wider frame repeats that lantern about fifteen times in two straight rows flanking the approach at even spacing, with the three torii being the same asset at three scales along one axis. No lean, no chip, no moss variant, no debris at any base. The same three foreground lanterns in `torii` are identical to each other.
findings.why: CRITIC.md priority 8: real places have clutter, wear and asymmetry. A perfectly regular row of identical props is the clearest signature of a level editor, and it is what makes the plateau read as a placement grid rather than a shrine that has stood for centuries.
findings.fix: Vary the repeated dressing. ACCEPTANCE on a re-shot phone/MEDIUM set: in the crop `shots/phone-wide-rN.png 0.4198,0.7795,0.1603,0.2000` the two visible lanterns must differ in yaw by at least 12 degrees and in height by at least 8%; at least one of the three foreground lanterns in `shots/phone-torii-rN.png` crop `0.0200,0.4400,0.3000,0.5000` must carry a distinct surface variant (moss, chip, lichen or soot) covering at least 15% of its visible area; and the along-approach spacing of the lantern row in `wide` must vary by at least 15% between consecutive gaps. GUARD: draw calls <= 140 and triangles <= 900k per ARCHITECTURE 7 -- the variation must come from per-instance attributes, not from new draw calls. CHECK PERFORMED: I cropped 0.4198,0.7795,0.1603,0.2000 at native and it contains exactly two stone lanterns on open plateau with no fence or torii in it, which is what the yaw/height criterion needs; per-instance yaw, scale and a variant index ride on an existing instanced draw, so the target and the draw-call guard are satisfiable simultaneously by construction with no new material or mesh.
findings.hypothesis: HYPOTHESIS, NOT A FINDING. The placement pass probably emits a fixed transform per slot with no jitter and no variant channel, rather than the variation existing and being overwritten. Check whether the instance buffer carries any per-instance rotation or scale at all before adding a variant system.
